ROUND-2 FINAL READ-ONLY REVIEW — PR #665, exact head a3943b51550d13a550bdc1cd59c03fd836bfe92c, scratch branch eshyra-olc5.12.11. Profile: rules-clause-complete / semantic-system. Reviewed the whole origin/main...HEAD diff (37 files), all four commits 9c0ed7b6, b205724d, 6a99d7e8, a3943b51, live PR body/checks, the requested live beads and follow-ups, faithful-or-absent, AGENTS.md, review/importer policies, ADRs 0017/0020, and applicable compiler guidance. refs/beads/state is stale (2026-09-09); live bd governed ownership and scope. Source checks used the vendored SRD PDF and actual pack, especially Conjure Elemental p.128, Efreeti Bottle/Elemental Gem pp.220-221, Figurines pp.221-223, and Ring p.235.

ROUND-1 DISPOSITION (original probes rerun before new adversarial probes):
S1 CLOSED for the declared source/instance/variant defect: real figurine grant memberships are source-correct; wrong variant, absent variant, dangling ref and ruling-with-grant declarations refuse. Schema and runtime enforce membership.
S2 original cases FIXED: all four vessels plus Elemental Gem require concentration and hand off to the uncontrolled successor; figurines forbid it; Ring uses ordinary removing cleanup. NOT closed across lifecycle consumers: S8 and S9 below.
S3 CLOSED for contradictory release cleanup: printed removal policies are derived and conflicting declarations refuse. The distinct last-actor departure/cooldown gap is S12 below.
S4 FIXED for both anchored carriers' original large-advance probes and the reported Ring owner-removal cascade: cooldowns use the effective termination minute and newly due resets settle in that advance. The broader expiry sweep has the new-successor gap S9 below.
S5 original grant and item-effect refresh probes FIXED: changed typed amount/unit/kind requires recorded override. NOT closed across the derived successor boundary (S8).
S6 CLOSED: Goat of Traveling binds with an adjudicated timed duration or until-removed without inventing a cap; the real pack's no-fixed-duration timer membership is the goat.
S7 original expiry/main life-event cases FIXED, but NOT closed across all callers: the character-condition projection inside start_effect still drops the resolver (S10).

REPAIR TABLE AUDIT:
Cascade enumeration in .12.10 is accurate for the existing recursive calls it lists: cleanup actor -> removeCombatantFromPlay -> breakCombatantConcentration carries eventElapsedMinutes; durable removal spreads it; condition removal through updateCampaignActor -> updateCombatant forwards it; character removeCondition and natural-form reversion do not call finalizeEnd; closeActorLinkAtZeroHp is a separate life-event entry. Explicit end, replacement, round/turn settlement and combat closure use their current event clock. However, the table does not establish settlement of a NEW due effect created by a cascade (S9).
Resolver enumeration: independently traced world advance/rest, begin-turn/round settlement, close-combat, combatant update/removal, HP/death-save/stabilize/suffocation/exhaustion tools, explicit end, refresh, target removal, concentration resolution, replacement and bonded-summon entry points. Their listed outer forwards are present, including the .12.10 additions. The toolStartEffect row is incomplete: replacement forwards input, but its nested addCondition call does not (S10). The 28-case parity matrix exercises replacement, not character-condition projection. Suppress/unsuppress, removeCondition, temp HP and clock-label updates do not themselves invoke terminal cleanup. Ebony Fly acceptance uses stat-block:giant-fly and works; its dedicated test covers refusal and 12-hour expiry.

S8 — P1 blocking — The as-spell lifetime is lost across successor creation and refresh.
Location: packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts:3255 (successor INSERT), :537 (itemBoundTypedDuration), :7125 (refresh validation).
Authority/invariant: .12 explicitly owns the elemental concentration exception, .12.6 S2/S5 requires the retained spell pointer and safe duration mutation, and SRD p.128 makes an uncontrolled elemental disappear one hour after summoning. Derived rows must preserve that binding; an admitted refresh must not make an ordinary later concentration break impossible.
Failure/evidence: with the unmodified bundled pack, bind Bowl at elapsed 0, voluntarily break concentration, then refresh_effect {effectId:'fx:uncontrolled', duration:{kind:'until-removed'}} with NO override. Accepted; after advance_time 120 the successor is active and elemental alive. Independently reproduced for Bowl, Brazier, Censer, Stone and Elemental Gem. createUncontrolledSuccessor preserves source_kind magic-item/source_ref but omits item_grant_json and duration provenance; the new refresh check therefore finds neither a grant nor effect binding and silently permits any duration. A sibling on the predecessor also fails: refresh Bowl to until-removed with the explicitly supported dm-adjudicated override succeeds, but the next voluntary concentration break fails and rolls back because createUncontrolledSuccessor still requires the original one-hour timed row. The same mechanism can refuse an owner life event. This is not excluded control/hostility interpretation.
Closure: preserve the resolved lifetime/identity and original summoning deadline through derived effects and every refresh; refuse incompatible mutations before committing or support their explicit override coherently without leaving a later break unexecutable. Permanent evidence: a generalized lifecycle invariant over the five real as-spell carriers, covering predecessor and successor refresh and successful later concentration/life-event cleanup. Proportionate to indefinite creatures and blocked state transitions; retain the exact SRD-backed deadline claim. Material repair; owner .12; repair/design reconciliation then fresh review.

S9 — P1 blocking — A cascade-created uncontrolled elemental is not expired in the time advance that crosses its deadline.
Location: packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts:7405 (one-time row snapshot), :7422 (cascade), :3255 (new successor).
Authority/invariant: .12's printed lifetime/reversion capability, SRD Conjure Elemental p.128, and ADR 0020 state integrity require the same settled game state for equivalent elapsed time partitions.
Failure/evidence: bind a real Bowl elemental at minute 0; a separate ruling summoning effect owns the concentrating combatant and expires at minute 30. advance_time 120 expires the owner effect, breaks concentration and creates fx:uncontrolled with deadline 60, but leaves that successor ACTIVE and the elemental ALIVE at minute 120. Advancing 30 then 90 instead ends the successor and makes the elemental ABSENT. Reproduced for all four vessels and Elemental Gem, with no readiness waiver or duration override. The existing sweep snapshots before the successor exists; processing the stale predecessor later cannot discover the new row. Threading the correct event minute does not settle it.
Closure: settle newly due lifecycle work created during the same advance, in effective-time order, while retaining idempotence and atomicity. Permanent evidence: generalized partition invariance over real as-spell grant carriers, including a cascade that creates a successor whose deadline also lies in the interval; compare creature presence and live effects, not only the cooldown counter. Material repair; owner .12. This is distinct from S8: no refresh is involved.

S10 — P1 blocking — start_effect's character-condition projection still loses the campaign resolver.
Location: packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts:5342; packages/core/src/state/domainMutations.ts:129.
Authority/invariant: S7 and .12.10 explicitly require every terminal/cascade caller to preserve the available exact campaign stack; ADR 0020 state integrity forbids refusing valid available bindings.
Failure/evidence: bind Bowl with a character concentrationOwner on base plus an available empty compatible review-addon. start_effect kind condition-package, source ruling, until-removed, conditions [{target:{kind:'character',ref:'pc-1'},condition:{id:'paralyzed'}} fails with "campaign rules pack 'dnd5e-srd' / 'review-addon' @ '1.0.0' is unavailable". The condition write rolls back, original concentration stays active, and no successor exists. The same call on base only succeeds. Reproduced with all five real elemental carriers without waivers; also reproduced for the paid Ring with only the spend-readiness waiver. The character addCondition context is rebuilt without input.resolveRulesPack, while adjacent combatant/campaign_actor branches forward it. The .12.10 matrix's start_effect case only tests concentration replacement and misses this branch.
Closure: finish S7's caller-class audit including nested mutations, and forward the resolver at this seam. Permanent evidence: extend the generalized base/add-on parity matrix with start_effect projecting an incapacitating condition onto the character owner, including an exceptional successor carrier and ordinary Ring cleanup. Proportionate to refusal of valid canon mutations; no need to duplicate every condition spelling. Material repair; owner .12; S7 is not closed.

S11 — P2 should-fix — Destroying the owning inventory instance strands an anchored grant and can lock time progression.
Location: packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts:3120; packages/core/src/state/itemState.ts:2009; packages/core/src/state/inventoryLifecycle.ts:64.
Authority/invariant: .12's new terminal anchor integration must coexist with authorized physical inventory destruction; ADR 0020 preserves atomic, executable state transitions. An effect must not require resurrection of a legitimately destroyed source just to terminate.
Failure/evidence: pay and bind Ring, then remove_item {id:ringId,disposition:'destroyed'} succeeds and deletes its inventory/state. advance_time 120 subsequently fails "inventory item ... does not match packRef ..."; clock rolls back to 0 and grant remains active. Explicit end_effect ruled also fails, so ordinary tools cannot terminate it. Independently reproduced with Efreeti serving grant. Both use the documented spend-readiness waiver only; the staged F5 integration is an accepted responsibility, with lower exposure reflected in P2. Dropping/selling preserves identity; full destruction is the relevant sibling. This is a state-integrity failure, not a request to automate excluded item death consequences or invent what a destroyed bottle does.
Closure: give destroyed-source grants a coherent terminal path (retained identity/tombstone or explicit destruction disposition as appropriate) without trying to schedule a nonexistent item's cooldown or blocking time/HP/end mutations. Permanent evidence: generalized source-instance lifecycle versus terminal cleanup for both anchored carriers, contrasting retained and destroyed instances and checking rollback only for real invalid inputs. Material repair; owner .12.

S12 — P2 should-fix — Removing the final granted actor through remove_effect_target delays its departure cooldown.
Location: packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts:6108 (partial link cleanup), :6203 (returns without a grant terminal transition), :3115 (anchor only in finalizeEnd).
Authority/invariant: the landed F5 grant-anchored capability must start the Ring wait after actual djinni departure (SRD p.235) and the stopper wait at the serving grant's return. An unlanded general F3 hook cannot hide a wrong positively landed F5 clock.
Failure/evidence: for both Ring and serving Efreeti, pay and bind the creature with its combatant also declared as an effect target. At minute 10 call remove_effect_target on that actor, reason ruled. It succeeds, applies remove cleanup and makes the creature absent, but the grant stays active and its depleted economy has NO availableAt. On advancing to minute 60 the empty effect expires and schedules availableAt 1500, rather than departure 10 + 1440 = 1450. Both carriers reproduced; spend readiness alone waived. The public tool's generic "never ends the effect" behavior needs a grant-specific admissibility/terminal decision here. This asks neither that all empty effects end nor that the excluded control policy be implemented.
Closure: make final-creature departure and its bound grant/anchor consistent, or refuse this partial-removal route for a bound grant and require the whole-grant end before changing state. Permanent evidence: generalized actor-departure/anchor-time invariant for both anchored carriers over whole-effect end, 0 HP, and final target removal, while preserving legitimate partial multi-actor behavior. Proportionate to newly claimed resource accounting; material repair; owner .12.

S13 — P2 should-fix — The new figurine admission loop exceeds CI's default test timeout.
Location: packages/core/test/itemGrantSummons.test.ts:989.
Authority/invariant: AGENTS.md requires all non-skipped tests to pass and proof machinery to have a proportionate, measured execution cost.
Evidence: pull_request CI run https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/actions/runs/38687266673 at EXACT head a3943b51550d13a550bdc1cd59c03fd836bfe92c fails build-test only because "S1 every figurine grant binds only to its own variant, and refuses an instance with no variant" times out at 5000ms. Log: 1 failed / 6839 passed / 18 skipped. The push run at the same head succeeds; the focused local run also passes, so this is a load-sensitive test-budget defect, not evidence that variant admission itself is wrong. The loop builds a full fresh DB/encounter for each grant and has no explicit timeout, unlike adjacent generalized carrier tests.
Closure/evidence: preserve the membership/admission assertions, amortize unnecessary setup or give this measured loop an appropriate local budget, then show full CI green under normal concurrency. No global timeout/worker-policy relaxation and no new permanent test of this test are required. Local test-only repair is non-material; the other findings still require fresh full review.

Surface this batch to the user/captain before any further repair authorization, as .12 and .olc5 require. Do not silently demote it or dispatch another example-only patch.
